heading: 1 OVERALL FINANCIAL RESULTS
start_phrase: Note: values may have been rounded
summary:
- Johnson & Johnson issued a press release detailing Q4 and full-year 2022 results and 2023 guidance.
- Q4 2022:
  - Reported sales declined 4.4% to $23.7B, primarily due to unfavorable foreign exchange and lower COVID-19 vaccine sales; operational growth excluding COVID-19 vaccine was +4.6%.
  - EPS fell 24.9% to $1.33; adjusted EPS rose 10.3% to $2.35.
- Full-year 2022:
  - Reported sales grew 1.3% to $94.9B, with operational growth of 6.1%, reflecting strong commercial execution partially offset by FX headwinds.
  - EPS decreased 13.8% to $6.73; adjusted EPS increased 3.6% to $10.15.
- 2023 guidance:
  - Adjusted operational sales growth excluding COVID-19 vaccine of 4.0%.
  - Adjusted operational EPS of $10.50, implying 3.5% growth.
- CEO commentary emphasized the strength and stability of all three business segments amid macroeconomic challenges and confidence in near-term growth and long-term value creation.
- Overall financial metrics (select):
  - Q4: Net earnings $3.52B; adjusted net earnings $6.22B.
  - FY: Net earnings $17.94B; adjusted net earnings $27.04B.
- Regional performance:
  - Q4: U.S. sales +2.9%; International -11.5% reported, with significant FX drag; worldwide -4.4% reported, +0.9% operational.
  - FY: U.S. +3.0% reported; International -0.6% reported but +9.1% operational; worldwide +1.3% reported, +6.1% operational.
- Segment performance (Q4):
  - Consumer Health: +1.0% reported, +6.4% operational.
  - Pharmaceutical: -7.4% reported, -2.5% operational (FX a major headwind).
  - MedTech: -1.2% reported, +4.9% operational.
- Non-GAAP notes: “Operational” excludes translational currency; “Adjusted operational” also excludes net M&A impacts; adjusted earnings exclude intangible amortization and special items.

summary:
- Overview of Johnson & Johnson’s full-year 2022 results versus 2021, with worldwide sales of $94.9B (+1.3% reported; +6.2% adjusted operational), and segment performance:
  - Consumer Health: $15.0B (-0.5% reported; +3.9% adjusted operational)
  - Pharmaceutical: $52.6B (+1.7% reported; +6.8% adjusted operational)
  - MedTech: $27.4B (+1.4% reported; +6.1% adjusted operational)
  - Notes clarify non-GAAP measures, exclusions for currency and M&A, and a reclassification of certain international OTC products from Pharmaceutical to Consumer Health.

- Segment commentary on growth drivers and headwinds:
  - Consumer Health: Growth led by OTC (TYLENOL, MOTRIN, upper respiratory, digestive health) and NEUTROGENA outside the U.S.; partially offset by international Oral Care softness.
  - Pharmaceutical: Growth driven by DARZALEX, STELARA, ERLEADA, TREMFYA, and long-acting INVEGA formulations; partially offset by declines in REMICADE, IMBRUVICA, and ZYTIGA.
  - MedTech: Strength in electrophysiology (Interventional Solutions), contact lenses (Vision), and wound closure (General Surgery).

- Notable quarterly announcements:
  - Regulatory: FDA clearance for DePuy Synthes TELIGEN System; FDA approval of TECVAYLI (teclistamab-cqyv) for relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma; BLA submitted to FDA for talquetamab in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma.
  - Clinical/data updates: Positive TREMFYA Phase 2b ulcerative colitis response (~80%); ASH 2022 presentations across hematology; Phase 3 PRECISION study shows aprocitentan reduces blood pressure in difficult-to-control hypertension; TREMFYA post-hoc analyses show early efficacy predicts long-term outcomes in psoriatic arthritis; CERENOVUS registry shows positive thrombectomy outcomes.
  - Corporate: CEO Joaquin Duato named Chairman; completion of Abiomed acquisition.

- Administrative note directing readers to SEC filings and investor websites for comprehensive disclosures.
text:
Pharmaceutical worldwide adjusted operational sales grew 6.8%*, driven by  DARZALEX (daratumumab), a 
biologic for the treatment of multiple myeloma, STELARA (ustekinumab), a biologic for the treatment of a number 
of immune -mediated inflammatory diseases,  ERLEADA (apalutamide), a next -generation androgen receptor 
inhibitor for the treatment of patients with prostate cancer, TREMFYA (guselkumab), a biologic for the treatment 
of adults living with moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, and for adults with active psoriatic arthritis,  and INVEGA 
SUSTENNA/XEPLION  and INVEGA  TRINZA/TREVICTA (paliperidone palmitate), long -acting, injectable 
atypical antipsychotics for the treatment of schizophrenia in adults.   This growth was parti ally offset by declines 
in sales of  REMICADE (infliximab), a biologic approved for the treatment of several  immune -mediated 
inflammatory diseases , IMBRUVICA (ibrutinib) , an oral, once daily therapy approved for use in treating certain 
B-cell malignancies, a type of blood or lymph node cancer , and ZYTIGA (abiratone acetate), an oral, once  daily  
medication for use in combination with prednisone for the treatment of metastatic castration -resistant prostate 
cancer .

progress. That’s why for more than 13 5 years, we have aimed to keep people well at every age and every stage

summary:
- Purpose: Reconciles Johnson & Johnson’s GAAP results to non-GAAP (adjusted) measures, by segment and consolidated, highlighting the impact of specific items on income before tax, margins, and net earnings.
- Scope and periods: Covers full year 2022 vs. 2021 and the fourth quarter of each year; includes both segment-level bridges and detailed line-item bridges for the consolidated P&L.
- Segments presented: Consumer Health, Pharmaceutical, MedTech, Unallocated, and Worldwide Total.
- Reported vs. adjusted income before tax (IBT):
  - Shows reported IBT and percent to sales for each segment and total.
  - Quantifies adjustments to derive adjusted IBT and adjusted percent to sales.
  - 2022 adjusted IBT totals approximately $31.9B (vs. $30.5B in 2021), with adjusted IBT margin ~33.6% (vs. ~32.5%).
- Key adjustment categories (quantified by segment and in the consolidated bridge):
  - Intangible asset amortization.
  - In-process research and development (IPR&D) charges.
  - Litigation-related items.
  - Losses/gains on securities (notably a loss in 2022 vs. a gain in 2021).
  - Restructuring-related items.
  - Acquisition, integration and divestiture related items (2022 includes Abiomed costs; 2021 includes gains on divestitures of two Pharmaceutical brands outside the U.S.).
  - Medical Device Regulation costs.
  - COVID-19 vaccine-related costs (notably in 2022).
  - Consumer Health separation costs and related tax items.
  - Other adjustments and tax legislation/other tax-related items.
- Consolidated GAAP-to-non-GAAP P&L bridges (quarter and year):
  - Reconciles cost of products sold, selling/marketing/admin, R&D, other income/expense, IPR&D, restructuring, provision for taxes, and net earnings from GAAP to non-GAAP for Q4 and full year 2022 and 2021.
- Notable disclosures/footnotes:
  - Prior-year reclassification: certain international OTC products (primarily China) moved from Pharmaceutical to Consumer Health based on operational changes.
  - Clarifies the nature of acquisition/divestiture adjustments (Abiomed in 2022; brand divestiture gains in 2021).
- High-level highlights:
  - Pharmaceutical segment carries the largest adjusted IBT; MedTech and Consumer Health also show adjustments primarily from amortization, restructuring, MDR costs, and separation-related costs.
  - Unallocated reflects Consumer Health separation costs and certain tax-related items.

summary:
- Purpose: Johnson & Johnson GAAP to Non-GAAP reconciliation (in millions) for the fourth quarter and full year periods ended Jan 1, 2023 and Jan 2, 2022.
- Scope: Reconciles key P&L line items—Cost of products sold; Selling, marketing and administrative expenses; Research and development expense; Other (income)/expense; In-process research and development; Restructuring; Provision for taxes on income; and Net earnings—from reported GAAP to adjusted Non-GAAP.
- Adjustment categories: Intangible asset amortization; Litigation-related; Restructuring-related; Medical Device Regulation; Consumer Health separation costs and related tax items; In-process R&D; Acquisition, integration and divestiture-related; (Loss)/gain on securities; COVID-19 vaccine-related costs; Tax legislation and other tax-related; and “Other.”
- Headline results:
  - Q4 2022 (ended Jan 1, 2023): GAAP net earnings $3,520; Non-GAAP net earnings $6,218.
  - Q4 2021 (ended Jan 2, 2022): GAAP net earnings $4,736; Non-GAAP net earnings $5,678.
  - FY 2022 (twelve months ended Jan 1, 2023): GAAP net earnings $17,941; Non-GAAP net earnings $27,038.
  - FY 2021 (twelve months ended Jan 2, 2022): GAAP net earnings $20,878; Non-GAAP net earnings $26,195.
- Notable effects:
  - Significant add-backs include intangible amortization, acquisition/integration/divestiture items, litigation, restructuring, Consumer Health separation, and tax-related adjustments.
  - “Other (income)/expense” shows large reclassifications after adjustments, at times turning expense into income.
  - In-process R&D and restructuring are treated as Non-GAAP adjustments (expensed in GAAP, removed in Non-GAAP).
- Footnote context: Acquisition, integration and divestiture-related items for 2022 primarily reflect Abiomed acquisition costs; 2021 includes gains from divestitures of two Pharmaceutical brands outside the U.S.
